meaning: To ruin something by overdoing it. The extra effort isn't just wasted — it spoils what was already finished.
So-so, careless, not great but not terrible. Also the standard modest answer when someone praises your Chinese.

literal: enter the village, follow its customs
meaning: When in Rome, do as the Romans do.
To kill two birds with one stone.
To contradict yourself. From a merchant selling an unstoppable spear and an unbreakable shield — a customer asked what would happen if he used one on the other.

literal: a frog at the bottom of a well
meaning: Someone whose view of the world is limited to their own small corner of it.

literal: guard the tree stump, wait for a rabbit
meaning: To wait for luck to strike twice instead of working. A farmer saw a rabbit run into a stump and die, so he stopped farming and watched the stump.

literal: mend the pen after the sheep are lost
meaning: Better late than never — fixing the problem after the damage is still worth doing.

literal: play the zither to a cow
meaning: To waste good material on an audience that can't appreciate it. Casting pearls before swine.

literal: give up halfway down the road
meaning: To abandon something before finishing it.
Half-hearted, unable to commit. Used for someone who can't decide or whose attention keeps wandering.
Absolutely perfect, flawless in every respect. Often used in the negative — nothing is 十全十美.

literal: a thousand methods, a hundred schemes
meaning: By every possible means; trying absolutely everything.
Living up to the name — genuinely as good as it's called.
Smooth sailing all the way. A standard well-wish for a new job, journey or venture.
Inconceivable, unbelievable — for things too strange or too impressive to take in.

literal: the heart's flowers burst into bloom
meaning: Bursting with joy.
Practice makes perfect.

literal: review the old, know the new
meaning: Revisiting what you already learned turns up something new. From the Analects — and a decent argument for reviewing your flashcards.

literal: paint the dragon, dot the eyes
meaning: The final touch that brings the whole thing to life. A painter added pupils to his dragons and they flew off the wall.

literal: the old man at the fort loses his horse
meaning: A blessing in disguise. His horse ran off, then returned with another; his son broke a leg riding it, which then kept him out of the army.
The road to anything worthwhile is full of setbacks.
Take your time, no rush. What you say to someone who's struggling and starting to panic.

pinyin: huó dào lǎo xué dào lǎo
literal: live until old, study until old
meaning: You're never too old to learn — keep studying as long as you live.

pinyin: yī fēn qián yī fēn huò
literal: one cent, one cent's worth of goods
meaning: You get what you pay for.

pinyin: bǎi wén bù rú yī jiàn
literal: hearing a hundred times is not like seeing once
meaning: Seeing is believing.
Wholeheartedly, with undivided attention.
To give something everything you have.
Before you realise it — for time that slipped past unnoticed.
Of course, naturally. Also for things taken for granted a little too easily.
Exactly alike, identical.
A complete mess. Works for rooms, schedules and situations alike.
Baffling. Often said of someone behaving oddly for no clear reason.
Unable to wait a moment longer.
In a few words — usually to say something can't be explained that briefly.

literal: a thousand words, ten thousand phrases
meaning: So much to say you don't know where to start.
It's a deal. Said to seal an agreement on the spot.
To mutter to yourself.
All saying the same thing; in unison.
Stunned speechless.

literal: to tell it is a long tale
meaning: It's a long story.

literal: the name is not falsely spread
meaning: It lives up to its reputation.
As everybody knows.
A household name; known to everyone.

literal: heard of by the whole world
meaning: World-famous.
Unknown, working away with no recognition.
To be unremarkable for years, then astonish everyone at once.

literal: the tip emerges from the bag
meaning: To stand out from the crowd. From an awl that can't stay hidden in a sack.
Head and shoulders above the rest.
One of a kind.
Distinctive, unlike everyone else.
Having a style all of its own.
Each has its own merits — no need to pick a winner.
Six of one, half a dozen of the other. Eight taels was half a catty.
Evenly matched.

literal: the difference of sky and earth
meaning: Worlds apart.
Completely different.
Much of a muchness; alike but for details.
Every kind under the sun; a wild variety.
Everything you could want is there.
A dazzling array — for a shop or display full of good things.
Too many to count.
Very few indeed.
So few you can count them on one hand.
Exceedingly rare and precious.

literal: hard to meet in a thousand years
meaning: A once-in-a-lifetime opportunity.

literal: the chance must not be lost
meaning: Don't let this opportunity slip.

literal: at the moment, decide at once
meaning: To make the call decisively when it matters.

literal: the urgency of the present task
meaning: The most pressing thing right now.

literal: pressing at the eyebrows and lashes
meaning: Extremely urgent; right in front of you.

literal: not a moment may be delayed
meaning: Admitting of no delay whatsoever.
Racing against the clock.

literal: new by the day, different by the month
meaning: Changing fast — for technology, cities, fields that move quickly.

literal: rising like steam, day by day
meaning: Going from strength to strength.
Making rapid progress by leaps and bounds.

literal: a thousand li in a day
meaning: Advancing at enormous speed.

literal: when the water comes, a channel forms
meaning: Do the groundwork and the result follows naturally.

literal: follow the logic, the essay writes itself
meaning: Following naturally from what came before.
Speaking with the confidence of someone who knows they're right.

literal: ask your heart, feel no shame
meaning: With a clear conscience.
Feeling entirely justified and untroubled about it.
Put yourself in their shoes.
To see it from the other person's side.

literal: feel it as if it happened to you
meaning: Deeply sympathetic, as though you'd been through it yourself.
So absorbed in work you forget to eat or sleep.
Round the clock, without stopping.
Working away tirelessly.
To keep at something over the long haul.
Persevering however slow the progress.
Unrelenting persistence.

literal: have a start, have an end
meaning: To see things through to the finish.
Methodical and well organised.
Step by step, in the proper sequence.
Down-to-earth; doing the unglamorous work properly.
To expect instant success without the climb.

literal: hungry for merit, close to profit
meaning: Chasing quick wins at the expense of what lasts.

literal: pull the shoots to help them grow
meaning: Ruining something by forcing it. A farmer tugged his seedlings taller; they died.

literal: wanting speed, you arrive at nothing
meaning: More haste, less speed.

literal: one day of sun, ten days of cold
meaning: Working in bursts with long gaps — the opposite of steady practice.
Not sure whether to buy it.
Utterly convinced.
Without question.

literal: a thousand true, ten thousand certain
meaning: Absolutely true — said when someone doubts you.

literal: wind comes from an empty cave
meaning: Rumours usually start somewhere. Now often used to mean the opposite — baseless.

literal: heard on the road, told on the way
meaning: Hearsay, picked up second-hand.
Repeat a lie often enough and it gets believed.

literal: what people say is to be feared
meaning: Gossip does real damage.

literal: all with eyes can see it
meaning: Plain for everyone to see.
Self-evident.
Clear at a glance.

literal: know it like your own palm
meaning: To know something inside out.

literal: a finished bamboo in the chest
meaning: To have a fully formed plan before starting. From painters who pictured the bamboo before lifting the brush.
To have a fair idea of where things stand.
Knowing perfectly well without saying so.
It goes without saying.
A shared understanding nobody needs to state aloud.

literal: the heart receives, the spirit grasps
meaning: To catch someone's meaning without explanation.
To take one example and work out the rest yourself.

literal: touch one kind, understand the neighbours
meaning: Understanding one thing opens up related ones.
To integrate everything you've learned into one working whole.

literal: broad in the old, fluent in the new
meaning: Deeply read in both history and the present day.

literal: learning enough to fill five carts
meaning: Enormously well read. Five cartloads of bamboo scrolls.
Exceptionally gifted.
Having character as well as ability.
Multi-talented.
Clever and good with their hands.

literal: the heart gets it, the hand obeys
meaning: So practised that it feels effortless.

literal: drive a light cart on a known road
meaning: Doing something you've done many times before.

literal: the blade moves with room to spare
meaning: Handling it easily, with capacity left over. From a cook whose knife found the gaps.
Mastery — the point where the craft is perfected.

literal: climb the peak, reach the summit
meaning: The very highest level attainable.
Superb to the point of seeming supernatural.
So lifelike it could breathe. Used of art and writing.
A remarkably faithful likeness.
Craftsmanship so fine it outdoes nature.
Refreshingly original.
Showing real ingenuity of design.
Breaking new ground; a new take on an old thing.
Looking completely refreshed.
Changed beyond recognition, usually for the worse.

literal: change the head, swap the face
meaning: A cosmetic makeover that leaves the substance untouched.

literal: shed the womb, swap the bones
meaning: A complete transformation, right down to the core.

literal: wash the heart, renew the face
meaning: To genuinely turn over a new leaf.
The wayward one comes good at last.
Pleasantly surprised — better news than you dared expect.
Beaming with delight.
In high spirits.
Full of eager interest.
With great relish — of eating, reading or listening.
Never tiring of something you love doing.
Finding something to laugh about in a rough patch.
The hard part is over and better days arrive.

literal: when the worst passes, fortune turns
meaning: Things improve once they've bottomed out.
A way out appearing just when the path seemed closed.

literal: the peak bends, the road turns
meaning: An unexpected turn for the better.

literal: find life in a hopeless place
meaning: Salvation arriving at the last possible moment.
A narrow escape from disaster.
To defuse a dangerous situation.
To pull through a crisis.
A scare that came to nothing.
Much panic over nothing.
On edge, braced for bad news.
Terrified.
Thrown into a panic and unable to act.

literal: hands and feet with nowhere to go
meaning: At a complete loss what to do with yourself.
At a loss.

literal: the six spirits have no master
meaning: So rattled you can't think straight.
Unable to settle; something is nagging at you.
Anxious and unsettled.
Too restless to keep still.

literal: watching until the eyes wear through
meaning: Waiting and waiting for someone to arrive.

literal: a day passes like a year
meaning: Time crawling during a miserable stretch.

literal: the heart homeward like an arrow
meaning: Desperate to get home.

literal: hoping the son becomes a dragon
meaning: Parents pinning big hopes on their child.

literal: swallow the bitter, chew the hard
meaning: Enduring hardship, usually for family.

literal: take the work, take the blame
meaning: Doing the thankless jobs without complaint.
Attentive to every last need.

literal: considerate down to the smallest thing
meaning: Thoughtful in the smallest ways.
Supporting one another through hard times. From stranded fish keeping each other alive.
Standing together through adversity.
Through thick and thin.

literal: one boat through wind and rain
meaning: In the same boat, weathering it together.
Pulling together.

literal: many wills build a city wall
meaning: Unity makes a group unbreakable.
A group with no cohesion at all.
Everyone doing their own thing, nobody coordinating.
Ploughing ahead regardless of what anyone advises.
Stubbornly refusing to reconsider.
Obstinate and deaf to advice — said of someone in charge.
Smugly certain you're correct.
Looking down on everybody.
Throwing your weight around.
Strutting about pleased with yourself.

literal: not to be matched in an age
meaning: Insufferably arrogant.
A small player convinced it's a major one. Yelang was a tiny kingdom that asked Han China which of them was bigger.
Everything in its proper place.

literal: a heart as open as a valley
meaning: Genuinely humble and open to others.
Modest and prudent.

literal: not ashamed to ask those below
meaning: Willing to ask questions of anyone, whatever their rank.

literal: see the worthy, think of matching them
meaning: Meeting someone better than you and resolving to catch up.
Learning from others to shore up your own gaps.
Leaning on what you're good at.
Teaching each student the way that suits them.

literal: suit the measures to the place
meaning: Adapting the approach to local conditions.
Treating the real problem rather than the symptom.

literal: measure the body, cut the cloth
meaning: Tailoring something to fit the case exactly.
All quiet; the trouble has passed.
On a grand, sweeping scale.
A perilous stretch — of a sea or a period in life.
With overwhelming force.
An earth-shaking change.
Momentous, world-shaking.
Deafeningly loud.

literal: not a crow or sparrow sounds
meaning: So quiet you could hear a pin drop.
The small hours, when everything has gone quiet.
A beautiful clear day.
Spring has arrived — also for any long-awaited good turn.

literal: riding high on a spring breeze
meaning: Flushed with success and enjoying it.

literal: ten thousand purples, a thousand reds
meaning: A riot of colour; a flourishing variety.
An idyllic spring scene.
Beautiful countryside.

literal: a peach spring beyond the world
meaning: An idyllic retreat far from everything. From a fisherman who stumbled on a hidden valley.

literal: mountains of people, seas of people
meaning: An enormous crowd.

literal: carriages like water, horses like dragons
meaning: Heavy, bustling traffic.
Crowded and noisy with people coming and going.
A place thronged with visitors.

literal: you could net sparrows at the door
meaning: So deserted you could catch birds on the doorstep.
Uninhabited wilderness.

literal: the sky's edge, the sea's corner
meaning: The ends of the earth.
From all directions.
From all over the country; all corners of the world.

literal: a thousand mountains, ten thousand rivers
meaning: A long and arduous journey.
Travelling over rough country to get somewhere.
Worn out from the road.

literal: the horse never stops its hooves
meaning: Without pause, straight on to the next thing.
To speed up something already moving quickly.
To come back with plenty to show for it.
To come away empty-handed.
All that work for nothing.
Everything achieved so far, wasted.

literal: the work fails by one basket
meaning: To fall at the final step. One last basket of earth would have finished the mound.

literal: failure on the verge of success
meaning: To collapse just as it was about to work.

literal: the great work is declared done
meaning: Finished at last.

literal: the work done, the name made
meaning: Having achieved both success and recognition.
To make your name overnight.

literal: step level into the blue clouds
meaning: To rise rapidly and smoothly through the ranks.
To rise fast in the world.

literal: falling a thousand zhang at once
meaning: A precipitous decline.

literal: each situation worse than the last
meaning: Going steadily downhill.

literal: the sun pressing on the western hills
meaning: Nearing its end; in terminal decline.

literal: the last of a strong crossbow's bolt
meaning: Spent force — powerful once, but out of momentum.

literal: danger within a day and a night
meaning: In imminent peril.
In a very shaky position.
On the verge of collapse.

literal: a thousand jun on one hair
meaning: Hanging by a thread; a hair's breadth from disaster.

literal: fight with the river at your back
meaning: To commit with no way to retreat. A general drew up his army against a river so nobody could flee.

literal: smash the cauldrons, sink the boats
meaning: To burn your bridges and commit absolutely.
To risk it all on a single gamble.

literal: driven to take a dangerous road
meaning: To take a desperate chance with no better option.
Out of options entirely.
At the end of your resources.

literal: hard to advance, hard to retreat
meaning: Caught between a rock and a hard place.

literal: difficult on the left and the right
meaning: In a dilemma whichever way you turn.

literal: riding a tiger, hard to dismount
meaning: Stuck in something you can't safely get out of.
Look before you leap.
Carefully thought through.
Thinking several moves ahead.

literal: bind the thatch before it rains
meaning: To prepare well before trouble arrives.

literal: guard against trouble before it forms
meaning: Prevention rather than cure.
Be ready and you have nothing to fear.

literal: sharpen the spear at the battle line
meaning: Last-minute cramming.

literal: knowing full well, doing it anyway
meaning: Breaking a rule you knew perfectly well.

literal: know the fault, fix it at once
meaning: Owning a mistake and correcting it.
Understand both sides before you act. From Sunzi.
To take victory with a move nobody saw coming.
A feint in one direction to attack in another.

literal: beat the grass, startle the snake
meaning: To tip off your target by acting carelessly.

literal: lead the wolf into the house
meaning: To invite in the very thing that will harm you.

literal: raise a tiger, breed a disaster
meaning: Tolerating a threat until it grows too big to handle.

literal: watch the fire from the far bank
meaning: To look on at someone else's trouble without helping.
To stand back and do nothing.
Help that arrives exactly when it's needed most.
A nice touch on something already good — pleasant, but not what anyone needed.

literal: drop stones on someone down a well
meaning: To kick a person while they're down.
To profit from someone else's crisis.
To bite the hand that fed you.
Ungrateful and disloyal.

literal: know the kindness, seek to repay
meaning: Grateful, and intending to return the favour.
To answer ill-treatment with kindness.
Tit for tat.
Going head to head, matching every point.

literal: lips like spears, tongues like swords
meaning: A fierce verbal duel.
Standing your ground on the merits.
Out of arguments because you were wrong.
Struck dumb, with nothing to say back.
Genuinely persuaded, not merely silenced.
To concede gracefully that someone is better.
Humbled by how much better someone else is.

literal: see their dust, never catch up
meaning: So far ahead you can only watch them go.
Looking poor by comparison.
Well matched opponents.

literal: the chess player meets their match
meaning: Finally facing someone at your own level.
Refusing to be outdone.
To pull yourself together and close the gap.

literal: the latecomer ends up on top
meaning: Starting behind and finishing ahead.

literal: blue comes from the indigo plant
meaning: The student surpasses the teacher.

literal: the young are to be reckoned with
meaning: Don't underestimate the next generation.

literal: old and all the stronger for it
meaning: Going strong in later life.

literal: the fine blade has not aged
meaning: Still got it, after all these years.

literal: build a household with bare hands
meaning: To start from nothing and build something.

literal: renew life by your own strength
meaning: Standing on your own feet.
To endure hardship deliberately while biding your time. A defeated king slept rough and licked a bitter gallbladder daily to keep his humiliation fresh.
To swallow humiliation for the sake of the larger task.

literal: hold the breath, swallow the voice
meaning: To put up with it in silence.

literal: endurance with nothing left to endure
meaning: Past breaking point.

literal: bear the pain, cut away what you love
meaning: To give up something you treasure.
Reluctant to say goodbye.
Unable to get something out of your mind.

literal: carved in bone, inscribed on the heart
meaning: Unforgettable, engraved on you.
As vivid as if it were yesterday.

literal: each one clear before the eyes
meaning: Still perfectly clear in the mind's eye.

literal: the things remain, the people do not
meaning: The place is unchanged but everyone has gone.
Things have moved on since then.
Time flies.

literal: sun and moon like a weaver's shuttle
meaning: The days and months shoot past.
A fleeting chance — let go for a moment and you've lost it.
A brief, brilliant flash that doesn't last.

literal: the days ahead are still long
meaning: There's plenty of time yet.
Boundless prospects.
A bright future ahead. A standard graduation wish.

literal: the great bird's flight of ten thousand li
meaning: Wishing someone a soaring career.
Full of promise, well worth pursuing.
Idling about with no occupation.
Loafing around avoiding work.
Allergic to hard work.
Getting something for nothing.
Reaping what others sowed.
Supporting yourself by your own work.
Comfortably provided for.
Living and working in peace.

literal: the state at peace, the people secure
meaning: A country at peace and its people content.

literal: draw a cake to fill the belly
meaning: Comforting yourself with something that isn't real.

literal: look at plums to quench thirst
meaning: Relief from imagination alone. A general told thirsty troops of plum groves ahead; their mouths watered and they marched on.

literal: a cup of water on a cartload of burning wood
meaning: A gesture far too small to make any difference.

literal: scratch an itch through the boot
meaning: Addressing something without ever reaching the actual problem.
Going in exactly the wrong direction for what you want.

literal: climb a tree to look for fish
meaning: Going about it in a way that cannot possibly work.

literal: trim the foot to fit the shoe
meaning: Mangling the substance to fit the form.

literal: cover your ears to steal a bell
meaning: Fooling nobody but yourself.
Kidding yourself, and trying it on everyone else too.
A clever move that backfires.

literal: the gain does not cover the loss
meaning: Not worth what it cost.

literal: lose the big over the small
meaning: Penny wise, pound foolish.

literal: abandon the root, chase the branch tip
meaning: Fussing over details while ignoring what actually matters.
Getting the priorities exactly backwards.
Two results from a single action.

literal: half the work, twice the result
meaning: Getting far more out of the effort.

literal: twice the work, half the result
meaning: Working twice as hard for half as much.
No trouble at all.

literal: as easy as turning your palm
meaning: Dead easy.

literal: as hard as climbing to heaven
meaning: Next to impossible.

literal: a thousand pains, ten thousand hardships
meaning: Untold difficulty and effort.
Having come through a great deal.

literal: grab the Buddha's feet at the last minute
meaning: Cramming the night before.

pinyin: jiāng hái shì lǎo de là
meaning: There's no substitute for experience.

pinyin: zhòng rén shí chái huǒ yàn gāo
literal: many gathering firewood make a high flame
meaning: Many hands make the fire burn bright.

pinyin: sān rén xíng bì yǒu wǒ shī
literal: among any three walking, one can teach me
meaning: There's something to learn from anyone. From the Analects.

pinyin: yǒu zhì zhě shì jìng chéng
literal: where there is will, the thing gets done
meaning: Where there's a will there's a way.

pinyin: shī bài shì chéng gōng zhī mǔ
literal: failure is the mother of success
meaning: You learn more from what goes wrong.

literal: the start is the hard part of everything
meaning: Getting going is always the hardest bit.

literal: a different trade is a mountain away
meaning: Outside your field, you know nothing.

pinyin: jiā jiā yǒu běn nán niàn de jīng
literal: every household has a scripture hard to recite
meaning: Every family has its own troubles.

pinyin: bù pà màn jiù pà zhàn
literal: fear not slowness, fear standing still
meaning: Slow is fine. Stopping is the problem.

pinyin: shuō cáo cāo cáo cāo dào
literal: speak of Cao Cao and Cao Cao arrives
meaning: Speak of the devil.

pinyin: yuǎn shuǐ jiù bù liǎo jìn huǒ
literal: distant water won't put out a nearby fire
meaning: Help too far away is no help at all.

pinyin: chē dào shān qián bì yǒu lù
literal: when the cart reaches the mountain there will be a road
meaning: It'll work itself out when you get there.

pinyin: yī cùn guāng yīn yī cùn jīn
literal: an inch of time is an inch of gold
meaning: Time is precious — and unlike gold, unbuyable.

pinyin: hǎo jì xìng bù rú làn bǐ tóu
literal: a good memory is worse than a bad pen
meaning: Write it down. You will not remember.

hanzi: 天下无难事只怕有心人
pinyin: tiān xià wú nán shì zhǐ pà yǒu xīn rén
literal: nothing under heaven is hard for the determined
meaning: Nothing is impossible to a willing mind.

hanzi: 台上一分钟台下十年功
pinyin: tái shàng yī fēn zhōng tái xià shí nián gōng
literal: a minute on stage, ten years of work off it
meaning: What looks effortless took years nobody saw.
